item.title: LLM Fatigue for the AI-Pilled
item.description:
Intro

My family has a few mottos. “Do Less” inspired by one of the greatest films ever (despite Russell Brand’s tarnished reputation. I consider the fact that he’s an ass in the movie to just be him playing himself) and “Life sucks, then you die”. I swear we’re actually a cheery lot. So what does this have to do with LLM burnout? Well, it feels like life is a lot more of the latter motto. Despite me writing the least amount of code in a year since high school, it feels like I’m doing more than ever as an IC. And I’m trying to figure out why. I’m going to share, in artisanally crafted words (no AI writing here), why I believe life sucks even for the most AI-pilled amongst us.

item.title: Flowwork
item.description:
Flowwork - An AI Coding Hardness

Background

I’m a fairly big believer in the power of GenAI for coding. I know there’s active debate in this area. If you’re not a fan of LLMs for coding, this blog may not be for you. Personally, I believe that humans will not write code for much longer (with some niche exceptions). For the current capabilities of LLMs, I do not think they’re good enough to “vibe-code” production level code. Harnesses that enforce strict coding standards with multiple, layered approaches to enforce them is essential. After almost a year of iteration, I’ve got “flowwork” in a good enough state where I feel comfortable writing about it. (Why “flowwork”? It was originally called workflow and I called v2 flowwork because I’m not creative.)
